newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds mixed after U.S. GDP data.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds mixed after U.S. GDP data.

text.p: Argentine bonds were narrowly mixed late morning Wednesday as fresh U.S. economic indicators put a dampener on a recent rally, analysts said.
"GDP figures in the United States came out very strong and this obviously could push interest rates up," said one trader at a foreign bank.
The U.S. government released strong gross domestic product growth data for the first quarter, which U.S. economists said could prompt the Fed to raise interest rates.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was up 1/4 at 91-3/4, the Par Brady bond was down 1/8 at 64-1/4, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 was unchanged at 126.00.
Another trader said the market did not seem nervous on today's news and was just waiting for more U.S. macroeconomic data due out this week before deciding how to trade.
"I believe that yesterday's good U.S. figures are still carrying this market, but there is no clear trend right now," he said.
"But with the U.S. economy growing as it is, we should probably expect some sort of rates adjustment in the medium-term."
